### 🎯 Today's Focus

Science.summary_markdown:
## Planning Fair Investigations: Control vs. Variable

- When planning an investigation, it helps to identify two things clearly before starting:
  - The **variable** -- the one factor you purposely change to see its effect.
  - The **control** -- the factors you deliberately keep the same, so the test is fair.
- Keeping everything the same except the one variable being tested means any difference in results can be fairly linked to that one factor.
- Example: for "Does water temperature affect how fast sugar dissolves?", the **variable** is the water temperature, while the **control** (kept the same) is the amount of sugar and the amount of water used each time.
- Example: for "Do gases have mass?", the **variable** is whether the balloon is inflated or not, while the **control** is using the same balloon and the same weighing scale for both weighings.
- A test is NOT fair if more than one factor changes at once -- for example, comparing ice melting in the sun (big cube) versus in the shade (small cube) mixes up two variables (location AND size), so you cannot tell which one caused any difference.

| Investigation | Variable | Control (kept the same) |
|---|---|---|
| Sugar dissolving | Water temperature | Amount of sugar, amount of water |
| Gases and mass | Balloon inflated or not | Same balloon, same scale |

- Planning the variable and control BEFORE running a test helps a student design a fair procedure from the start, instead of discovering problems only after the results come in.

quiz.question: In an investigation, what is the "variable" that is being purposely changed to see its effect?
options: The one factor the investigator changes on purpose
quiz.correct_answer: The one factor the investigator changes on purpose

quiz.question: In an investigation, what is a "control" or something "kept the same"?
options: The factors that are kept unchanged so the test is fair
quiz.correct_answer: The factors that are kept unchanged so the test is fair

quiz.question: Why must an investigation keep most factors the same except the one being tested?
options: So that any difference in results can be fairly linked to the one factor that was changed
So the investigation takes less time
Because it is required by the materials list
It does not matter which factors are kept the same
quiz.correct_answer: So that any difference in results can be fairly linked to the one factor that was changed

quiz.question: In the question "Does water temperature affect how fast sugar dissolves?", what is being changed on purpose (the variable)?
In the same investigation, "Does water temperature affect how fast sugar dissolves?", what should be kept the same (a control) for a fair test?
options: The amount of sugar and the amount of water used each time
Nothing needs to be kept the same
quiz.correct_answer: The amount of sugar and the amount of water used each time

quiz.question: A group plans to test "Do gases have mass?" by weighing a balloon before and after inflating it. What is the variable in this plan?
options: Whether the balloon is inflated (has gas) or not
The brand of the weighing scale
quiz.correct_answer: Whether the balloon is inflated (has gas) or not

quiz.question: For "Do gases have mass?", which should stay the SAME between the two weighings to make it a fair test?
options: The same balloon and the same weighing scale
The size of the balloon should change each time
A different scale for each weighing
The room should change each time
quiz.correct_answer: The same balloon and the same weighing scale

quiz.question: A group testing sugar dissolving plans to use warm water in one cup and cold water in another, both with the exact same amount of asukal (sugar) and the exact same size of cup. Is this a fair test?
options: Yes, because only the water temperature differs while other factors are kept the same
No, because the cups are the same size
No, because sugar was used in both cups
Yes, but only because it uses two cups
quiz.correct_answer: Yes, because only the water temperature differs while other factors are kept the same

quiz.question: A group planning an investigation about dissolving sugar decides to use warm water in a big glass and cold water in a small cup, with different amounts of sugar in each. What is wrong with this plan?
options: Too many factors are different (container size and sugar amount), so it will not be clear which factor caused any difference
The plan needs a hotter temperature
Nothing is wrong since it still uses water and sugar
quiz.correct_answer: Too many factors are different (container size and sugar amount), so it will not be clear which factor caused any difference

quiz.question: When writing a procedure for testing "Do gases have mass?", which step should come first?
options: Weigh the empty (deflated) balloon and record its mass
Compare the two results and write a conclusion
Record the findings in a table
quiz.correct_answer: Weigh the empty (deflated) balloon and record its mass

quiz.question: After testing, a group finds sugar dissolved in 20 seconds in warm water and 85 seconds in cold water, using the same amount of sugar and water both times. What conclusion is best supported by this finding?
options: Warmer water makes sugar dissolve faster, based on the clear difference observed under otherwise identical conditions
The type of cup used determined the dissolving speed
Sugar dissolves at the same rate no matter the temperature
The results cannot be trusted because only one trial was done
quiz.correct_answer: Warmer water makes sugar dissolve faster, based on the clear difference observed under otherwise identical conditions

quiz.question: Why is it important for a student to name the control and the variable BEFORE running an investigation, rather than deciding afterward?
options: Planning this ahead of time helps the student design a fair procedure and know exactly what to keep the same, instead of realizing too late that other factors were also changing
It is not important, since conclusions can be written no matter how the test was run
Naming these afterward always gives the same accurate results
Only the conclusion needs to be planned in advance
quiz.correct_answer: Planning this ahead of time helps the student design a fair procedure and know exactly what to keep the same, instead of realizing too late that other factors were also changing

quiz.question: A student designs a test comparing how fast paper towels absorb tubig (water) versus tissue paper, using the same amount of water, the same size of paper, and the same pouring method for both. What makes this a strong, fair investigation plan?
options: Only one factor (the type of paper) is different, while everything else that could affect the result is kept the same
It uses two different types of paper, which is enough on its own
It does not need a written procedure since the materials are simple
It compares two liquids instead of two materials
quiz.correct_answer: Only one factor (the type of paper) is different, while everything else that could affect the result is kept the same

quiz.question: A student proposes the testable question, "Does the amount of asukal (sugar) affect how sweet a glass of calamansi juice tastes?" What would be the variable, and what would need to be kept the same?
options: The variable is the amount of sugar added; the amount of juice, water, and calamansi used should be kept the same
The variable is the type of glass used; nothing else matters
The variable is the temperature; the amount of sugar should change too
There is no variable in this question
quiz.correct_answer: The variable is the amount of sugar added; the amount of juice, water, and calamansi used should be kept the same

quiz.question: A group wants to compare how fast ice melts in the sun versus in the shade. They use a big ice cube in the sun and a small ice cube in the shade. Why can't they trust their results to answer their original question fairly?
options: Because the size of the ice cubes is different, so they cannot tell if the sun/shade or the size caused any difference in melting speed
Because ice always melts at the same speed everywhere
Because sun and shade are the same temperature
Because the investigation has too many materials
quiz.correct_answer: Because the size of the ice cubes is different, so they cannot tell if the sun/shade or the size caused any difference in melting speed
